title: Max Gordon thanks him for hitting his brother-in-law
summary: The owner of the Vanguard was delighted and refurbished the club overnight.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I'm on the bandstand the next night, Max Gordon walks

in. I say oh-oh, he's going to bring me the bill. As well as he and I got along, you know, I say he's going to bring me the bill. He sit there until I got off the bandstand. Called me over. I sit down beside him. As soon as I sit down beside him, he threw his arms around my shoulder, (laughter) and shooked my hand and thanked me for tearing up the club and kicking his brother-in-law. That's the part that got it. Otherwise, I'd of had to pay for everything in there. If I hadn't of done something to his brother-in-law, he'd never of forgiven me. One thing that I did to his brother-in-law, he wanted to do all his life.

So he stayed there all night buying me drinks. And he's just laughing all night long. He say I can just see him on one side going across the room. (Laughter). He said, 'did he get up in a hurry, John?' I say 'no, he didn't get up in a hurry.' He wanted to know what did he do after that? I say he went back into the kitchen. (Laughter). Oh, he just laughed all night long. Bought the band drinks. Oh, he was real happy.

But the next night he had the place refurbished with tables and chairs and whiskey. But he was sure glad that I whipped his brother-in-law. And I was glad that he was glad to because I didn't have to pay for anything.
I thought that when you told me this story before, you said that, Lady was there that night?

I stand to be corrected. Yeah, so Monty Kaye and I say our group, we was fighting for dear life, you know, busting chairs over heads and things, turning over tables, throwing the chairs in the whiskey. Boy that was a blow out.
